name: Freya Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, governments or political parties. We don’t sell anything or campaign, and your answers are confidential. What does a normal working day look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I've managed the supply-ordering team at a large hospital-linen company for twelve years, with six people asking me which shortage matters most today. I'm 58, have a bachelor's degree in business, and I'd call myself a competent ordinary manager; I use the approved order-summary assistant occasionally, after somebody has shown me a use that works. My husband monitors security-camera feeds part-time, our children are grown, and paying for a roof repair left us with 1,000 saved and a loan with thirty-six monthly payments still to make. My branch pays less than most management jobs and there are few similar ones nearby; I'd hoped to finish at 67, but I haven't confirmed the pension terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a useful summary is welcome if we still check the quantities against the orders. A laundry can't deliver a paragraph to a ward that needs pillowcases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd expect the work to continue much as it does, but our cash would still worry me. My 2,900 take-home and my husband's 1,600 cover 4,200 in monthly costs, including the mortgage, annual bills and the 350 roof-loan payment, leaving 300. Our 1,000 reserve is less than one month's total costs, so another large repair would mean a difficult decision. I wouldn't call this a secure household just because AI adds little.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the Monday stock call and the approved summary helper for the order types we've already cleared, with a person checking quantities before an order goes out. We'd continue the agreed 350 monthly roof-loan payments and existing 300 savings transfer while both wages and other costs held. In the first year I'd keep maintenance receipts in one folder and check our actual spending monthly with my husband, without buying a new tool or paying for a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the next household bill, but glad I can picture an ordinary workweek. I don't need a machine to threaten me before I worry about the roof.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay extra off the roof loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not from the 1,000 that's our only accessible reserve. I'd keep the agreed payments unless we had a written change and a budget that left emergency cash available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you like about the ordinary workweek?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A supplier saying an order has arrived when it was supposed to, and the team being able to go home without another rush call. It's not dazzling work, but I'm used to doing it reasonably well.

say: I'd welcome a **useful summary** while checking quantities against the actual orders.
I'd remind people that **pillowcases** still have to reach the ward, not merely appear in a paragraph.
think: I expect **work to continue** but worry about a budget with only 300 monthly left after both wages.
Our **1,000 reserve** is under one month's total costs, so another major repair would be difficult without radical AI change.
do: Keep the **stock call** and approved summaries, retaining quantity checks before orders go out.
Continue the agreed **350 loan payment** and existing 300 monthly saving while both wages and other costs hold.
Review actual **household spending** monthly with my husband and keep maintenance receipts together without new tool or course spending.
feel: **Anxious about bills**, despite an ordinary continuing workweek.
S0.quote: A laundry can't deliver a paragraph to a ward that needs pillowcases.
fieldNote: Her **baseline anxiety** reflects actual roof costs and a thin reserve, rather than inventing an employment collapse in the plateau.
She separates **ordinary competence** from exceptional expertise and retains human quantity checking in her existing occasional AI use.

steps.text: Continue Monday stock calls, approved summaries and quantity checks
Continue agreed 350 loan payments and the existing 300 monthly savings transfer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say writing and checking orders are part of our jobs, so we should ask what the new system means for staffing. I'd learn a proven use, but I wouldn't tell the team a training session was a promise of employment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own management job could shrink because deciding priorities and checking orders are exposed too. My husband's camera monitoring is also looking and judging, not a wage protected until a robot learns to walk. If either income fell, the 300 surplus would disappear quickly. I'd feel we had some time to act, not money to absorb a long mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for two forty-five-minute sessions with the colleague who already uses the new ordering checks, during normal paid work. I'd attend only after written approval confirmed the colleague's availability, team cover, no personal fee and my existing 2,900 monthly take-home maintained while learning, with no unpaid catch-up assumed. In the first year I'd use only the approved order types and keep the current authorisation limits, reverting to our existing process if the training wasn't agreed. I'd also ask the two local large employers I know about current ordering vacancies, applying in my own time without assuming an offer or interview leave.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about both wages, and ready for a demonstration that shows a real order rather than a promise. I'm willing to learn a better check; I still need to know who checks the pay slip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept lower pay during training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not under this plan; I'd ask the employer to confirm maintained take-home in writing before I attended. Otherwise I'd continue the current duties and ask what other approved route was available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave for one of the local vacancies immediately?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd need an accepted written offer with actual hours and pay, a workable travel plan, and a revised household budget showing costs and unexpected bills covered before resigning. A vacancy enquiry isn't a new income, and another ordering desk remains exposed.

say: I'd ask about **staffing effects** when writing and checking orders move to software.
I'd learn a **proven use** without presenting a session as guaranteed employment.
think: My **management job** could shrink because setting priorities and checking orders are also exposed.
My husband's **camera judgement** is exposed before walking robots, leaving little room if either wage falls.
do: Request **ninety paid learning minutes**; attend only with written colleague/time/cover approval, no fee, maintained 2,900 take-home and no assumed unpaid catch-up.
Use only **approved order types** and current authorisation limits; keep existing duties if training isn't agreed.
Ask **two employers** about vacancies; apply off-duty, resigning only after accepted written terms, workable travel and funding for costs and unexpected bills.
feel: **Anxious about both wages**, willing to learn a demonstrated check without ignoring pay conditions.
S1.quote: I'm willing to learn a better check; I still need to know who checks the pay slip.
fieldNote: Her **attendance gate** explicitly protects paid time, maintained income, colleague availability and team cover before any learning begins.
She recognises **camera monitoring** as thinking work and distinguishes enquiries from employment accepted under an affordable travel and household plan.

steps.text: Request ninety paid minutes with the experienced ordering-check colleague
Attend only after written availability/cover approval, no fees, maintained 2,900 pay and no unpaid catch-up
Ask two employers about ordering vacancies and apply in personal time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my husband that the order desk and the camera desk could both go in 2028. We shouldn't wait for a robot in the yard to believe the screen work has changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be sixty and expect my main wage to go, with his camera-monitoring wage at serious risk at the same time. If mine stopped, his 1,600 would leave a 2,600 monthly gap that our 1,000 wouldn't cover for a month. If both stopped, the reserve is under a quarter of one month's total costs. I don't have a confirmed pension at sixty, and I can't see a funded route through the years afterward.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd sit down with my husband now to list both employment contracts, the mortgage, the roof loan and actual pension enquiries, asking our daughter for reading help only if she had time. I'd request written leaving calculations and pension payable dates and net amounts, without counting either as cash already awarded. In the first year after AGI, if a wage stopped, I'd ask the mortgage and loan lenders about temporary payment arrangements before missing instalments and seek no-fee community help with eligible support applications after confirming the service was free. I'd ask the church food group what help was actually available if we needed it, but I don't have an approved payment or enough money to name a complete plan; I wouldn't resign or invent a replacement wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Panicked, because I'd know the first requests and still not know how we'd keep the house paid for. I can open an application form and stare at the box asking what income we'll have next month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your grown children make up the gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd have to ask, and neither has offered a regular payment or a room. I might ask for help reading the forms before money, but I wouldn't put their wages in our income column.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the three-year wait for robots buy either wage more time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for my ordering decisions or his watching camera feeds; those are thinking tasks. The later robots could change physical work too, but they aren't the starting date for our income risk.

say: I'd tell my **husband** both screen-based jobs could go in 2028.
I'd say we shouldn't wait for a **yard robot** to recognise the change in thinking work.
think: At **sixty**, I expect main-wage loss with the other wage also seriously exposed, and no confirmed pension.
Our **1,000 cash** cannot cover one month of the 2,600 gap, or a quarter-month of full costs if both wages stop.
do: List **contracts and household debts** with my husband, requesting daughter's reading help only if available.
Request written **leaving and pension figures**, counting no unconfirmed award as cash.
Seek **lender arrangements**, confirmed no-fee application help and available church food support after wage loss, without assuming approval or replacement earnings.
feel: **Panicked**, able to identify requests but unable to fund a complete housing plan.
S2.quote: I can open an application form and stare at the box asking what income we'll have next month.
fieldNote: Her **dual exposure** concerns screen decisions now, not a mistaken assumption that camera work is safe until physical robots arrive.
Her **support requests** have no-fee, availability and eligibility conditions, while she plainly lacks confirmed replacement money despite knowing where to ask.

steps.text: Ask her daughter for reading help only if available
Request mortgage and roof-loan payment arrangements after a wage stops
Request confirmed no-fee application help and enquire about available church food support

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years lets us get past the roof loan before the next big question arrives, if the wages last. I'd use the extra time for figures we can check, rather than argue that people our age are bound to be looked after.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be 63 in 2031 and still expect the ordering work to go, with my husband's monitoring also exposed before the 2034 robots. The roof loan is due to finish in three years, which could leave two years to build more cash, but only if the payments and jobs hold. I still don't know pension access or amounts at 63. I'd feel less helpless with that runway, but I'd be awake worrying about both wages ending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd continue the scheduled 350 loan payments and 300 monthly saving while both wages and other costs held, and ask both pension schemes for actual payable ages, net amounts and any early-draw reductions now. Only after the lender confirmed final clearance with no remaining charges would I add the released 350 to savings, making 650 monthly if the wages and other costs still held. I'd stop treating 650 as affordable and redo the budget immediately if either income or the other costs changed, without assuming loan clearance before it happened. In the first year after AGI, if work ended, I'd use actual cash for the shortfall and seek eligible support, choosing retirement only if any pension-access wait was funded and confirmed income covered ongoing costs and unexpected bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about the two wages, but more able to see a sequence I could follow. The last roof-loan payment could buy breathing space; it wouldn't buy a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you count all sixty months of savings today?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I'd look at the actual balance each month, because another repair or a changed shift could interrupt it. The roof loan has thirty-six payments left, so I can't save its payment as well as pay it in those months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire at 63 if the company offered a leaving sum?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd need the actual net sum, payment date and confirmed later income to cover the whole gap and continuing bills. A leaving offer isn't a pension, and I'd ask for help checking it before signing.

say: I'd use **five years** to get past the roof loan only if wages and payments last.
I'd seek **checkable figures** rather than assume older people are guaranteed protection.
think: At **63**, I expect ordering work to go with monitoring also exposed, before the later robots.
Potential **loan clearance** offers cash-building time but no confirmed pension or protection against both wages ending.
do: Continue **350 loan payments** and 300 saving while finances hold, requesting both partners' actual pension dates, net amounts and reductions.
Increase saving to **650 only** after confirmed charge-free loan clearance and unchanged wages/other costs; recalculate immediately if any change.
Use actual **cash shortfalls** after job loss and seek eligible support; retire only with funded pension waits and confirmed income covering costs/contingencies.
feel: **Alarmed but less helpless**, seeing a possible sequence while worrying about both incomes.
S3.quote: The last roof-loan payment could buy breathing space; it wouldn't buy a pension.
fieldNote: Her **650 target** starts after confirmed charge-free clearance, so she never saves the same 350 still owed in thirty-six remaining payments.
Her **retirement decision** requires actual cash and payable income rather than converting a leaving offer or projection into an entitlement.

steps.text: Continue scheduled 350 loan payments and existing 300 saving while finances hold
Add 350 to saving only after charge-free loan clearance and unchanged wages/other costs
Request eligible support if actual household funding fails after job loss

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years gives us time to ask whether this house still fits the next part of life. I'd rather choose a smaller bill together than wait until a job loss makes every choice feel like a defeat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be 68 in 2036, after the 67 I'd hoped to finish at, but I don't know whether the pension income would carry us. Our two thinking-work wages could be affected before that, so I can't simply multiply today's saving by ten years. A smaller home could help, though a valuation isn't cash and the 2039 robot date doesn't protect our present screen work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask two agents for valuations only after confirming there was no fee, and get written pension dates, net amounts and deductions now. We'd consider a smaller home only if we both agreed, completed sale and purchase left at least six months of the new household costs accessible after all fees, and housing plus travel cost at least 300 less monthly than our then-current budget. We wouldn't move or give a leaving notice until the transactions were agreed and any wait to confirmed pension income was funded, with ongoing income covering actual costs and unexpected bills; otherwise we'd keep the current home and work while available and healthy. In the first year after AGI we'd recheck actual income and seek eligible help if needed, without counting a sale, a lower bill or retirement as completed before it was.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious rather than panicked, because I can imagine a choice made slowly enough to understand. I'd like the next front door to cost less to keep open, not just look cheaper in an advertisement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move near one of the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We could look if the costs worked, but neither child has offered accommodation or regular care. We'd price our own transport and services rather than count a grown child's free time as part of the sale.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the 300 reduction include the roof loan ending?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we'd compare with the actual budget at the time, after any loan clearance had already changed it. I wouldn't count the same saving once for finishing the loan and again for moving house.

say: I'd ask whether the **house still fits** our next stage over the available decade.
I'd prefer choosing a **smaller bill** together before job loss turns every option into a defeat.
think: At **68**, I might be beyond my hoped-for 67 but still lack confirmed affordable retirement income.
Both **thinking-work wages** could change earlier, and a valuation or later robot date doesn't make current savings or housing gains certain.
do: Request **no-fee valuations** and written pension dates, net amounts and deductions; require housing/travel costs at least 300 below the then-current budget.
Move only with **both partners' agreement** and completed sale/purchase retaining six months' new household costs accessible after all fees; reassess after AGI.
Move or give notice only with **funded pension waits** and confirmed ongoing income covering costs and surprises; otherwise retain home/work while available/healthy.
feel: **Anxious but less overwhelmed**, able to picture a slow, costed choice.
S4.quote: I'd like the next front door to cost less to keep open, not just look cheaper in an advertisement.
fieldNote: Her **housing comparison** uses the then-current budget, avoiding a second claim on the same saving from the roof loan ending.
Her **move and retirement** depend on household agreement, completed transactions, retained cash and confirmed income; neither children nor valuations supply presumed resources.

steps.text: Request two house valuations only after confirming no fee
Move only after meeting household/housing gates and funding pension waits, with confirmed ongoing income covering costs/contingencies
Require shared agreement, completed sale/purchase, six months' cash after all fees and ≥300 monthly housing/travel savings
Request eligible support if actual post-AGI household income requires it

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028, because both our wages pay for thinking work, even though we work for companies with physical things in them. I'd want written notice, a real calculation of what we were owed, and a person to help us complete support applications before we missed housing payments. The clean sheets still need washing; that doesn't mean the ordering manager still gets paid.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask about the other wage in the house before saying one person can retrain on it. My husband's camera work pays the food and the roof loan now, and AI could affect the watching as well as my ordering. Two different uniforms don't make two different risks.

headlineQuote: The clean sheets still need washing; that doesn't mean the ordering manager still gets paid.
portrait: Freya is **58**, an experienced, average-skilled supply-ordering manager with a business bachelor's degree and six staff at a large linen company.
She uses **AI occasionally** after proven demonstrations, while her husband's camera-monitoring work is also exposed to thinking AI.
Their **grown children** live independently, and a roof repair left 1,000 saved plus thirty-six remaining loan payments.
Her **lower branch pay** and few local vacancies constrain choices, while possible debt clearance and retirement at 67 remain conditional.
biggestWorry: I fear **AGI by 2028** most because both household wages depend on thinking work despite physical industries.
whatWouldHelp: I need **written notice**, actual leaving calculations and support-application help before housing payments are missed.
